paragraphs.dominant_move: urgency: Faster recovery can support rescue and closure. -> sets the ranked human objective -> moves to location and route inputs
model-route: Crash-state and search-plane inputs can support route simulation. -> defines the modeling route -> moves to the search field
location-field: A bounded Gaussian field represents where to look. -> creates a common target distribution -> supports ideal route comparison
ideal-comparison: Systematic routes reduce redundancy under perfect discovery. -> identifies a geometric candidate -> introduces imperfect detection
uncertainty-update: Bayesian updating retains fast median search with missed detections. -> promotes an adaptive route -> tests flexibility
transfer: The framework can change aircraft count and target size. -> claims bounded flexibility -> moves to recommendation
recommendation: Bayes is the preferred realistic procedure. -> states the decision -> the body must justify it
context-and-stake: Modern tracking does not eliminate open-ocean disappearance. -> establishes need -> ranks objectives
ranked-objectives: Discovery comes first and rescue time second. -> creates the decision rule -> adds entity variation
research-route: Cases, communication, search theory, sensors, variables, and geometry must be established before paths. -> defines the evidence foundation -> moves to simulation
validation-to-decision: Ideal routes should be tested, made less ideal, transferred, analyzed, and then recommended. -> commits to an auditable decision route -> research begins the route

global_organization_chain: human urgency and ranked success criteria
Only after the positive language, organization, model, and visual chain is complete does G7 record notation, statistics, calibration, fact, and provenance warnings.

moves: input: An aircraft missing over remote water, rescue urgency, uncertain crash location, and finite search resources.
rhetorical job: Make the whole paper legible as an escalation from location prediction and ideal route screening to imperfect discovery and a final decision.
analytical job: Preview a bounded Gaussian location field, random and systematic route simulations, Bayesian updating, completion proportions, and transfer to different targets/resources.
output: A conditional promise that posterior-guided searching can find most modeled crashes quickly enough to matter for rescue.
handoff: The contents and introduction unpack the research, assumptions, candidate routes, realism upgrade, evidence, and recommendation.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The summary's location-to-route-to-recommendation promise.
rhetorical job: Expose the unusually long evidence route before the reader enters historical research or simulation detail.
analytical job: Order research, variable/scenario foundation, assumptions, two model regimes, stability tests, comparative results, recommendation, public communication, and provenance.
output: A complete source-heading map in which ideal and uncertainty-aware solutions remain visibly distinct.
handoff: Introduction supplies the ranked human criteria that give this architecture its decision purpose.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Modern aircraft can still disappear over open ocean while families and possible survivors wait.
rhetorical job: Rank success criteria and show that the proposed recommendation will be earned through a declared sequence rather than asserted immediately.
analytical job: Prioritize discovery, then rescue time; include aircraft/sensor variation; route case research, variables, geometry, simulation, imperfect detection, stability, and analysis.
output: A two-level objective and an auditable research-to-decision work plan.
handoff: Historical and technical research select the incident class, lost-plane trigger, probability objective, and sensor regime.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A broad class of ocean disappearances with heterogeneous aircraft, causes, communication systems, and search technologies.
rhetorical job: Narrow the modeling case through explicit historical, geographic, causal, regulatory, and sensing choices.

analytical job: Use Earhart/MH370 as context; screen 89 cases; choose Atlantic passenger aircraft and three representatives; exclude ATC/hijacking cases; set a 30-minute uncertainty interval; define containment times detection; choose P-8 radar.
output: A modelable Atlantic mid-flight crash case with a representative target set, lost-contact window, probability objective, and initial ideal sensor.
handoff: Variables and scenario calculations translate those research choices into geometry and simulation parameters.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The selected incident class, representative aircraft, 30-minute alert rule, search-theory probabilities, and P-8 radar.
rhetorical job: Bind every later equation and path rule to named physical or operational quantities before simulation begins.

analytical job: Define lost/search states; derive glide range and 30-minute path length; create a swept-capsule rectangle; select Boeing 777 values; simplify containment to uniform x and normal y; choose P-8 speed and sight.
output: A 520-by-200-mile coordinate search field, probability representation, selected target/search aircraft, and symbol interface.
handoff: General assumptions freeze the regime in which these inputs may be used.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The rectangle, containment model, representative aircraft, sensor, and search-time objective.
rhetorical job: Make the first experiment's idealizations inspectable and organize them by environment, crash, and search operation.
analytical job: Fix flat geometry, no wind/current, on-route instantaneous failure, bounded glide, stationary debris, ideal mobilization/endurance/weather/cost, and uniform radar sight.
output: A controlled ideal regime whose known gaps can later motivate discovery uncertainty and final limitations.
handoff: The normal-distribution model instantiates the common crash generator, completion rule, and statistical protocol.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: A rectangular normal-containment field, ideal radar, search-plane motion variables, and candidate route requirement.
rhetorical job: Give every route a shared test bed and reporting template so comparisons do not change the target or stopping rule.
analytical job: Sample crashes from the normal field; stop when distance is below sight range; summarize time by mean, median, spread, standard error, and 95-percent confidence interval.
output: A reusable simulation harness and comparison metric for ideal-discovery paths.
handoff: Random paths establish failure, confinement, and weighting baselines within that harness.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The shared crash field, ideal completion rule, P-8 speed/sight, and a need for a comparison baseline.
rhetorical job: Reveal why unconstrained randomness, boundary confinement, and weak containment weighting remain inadequate.
analytical job: Update a random unit vector; redirect excursions orthogonally; add endpoint weighting; run 100 trials where feasible; compare skewed time distributions and overlapping intervals.
output: An unviable unbounded route and two slow, redundant bounded baselines with no proven difference between them.
handoff: Systematic routes directly repair overlap and probability-ordering failures.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: Random-route redundancy, a normal containment field, 10-mile sight, and the common ideal-detection harness.
rhetorical job: Make each new geometry a traceable repair and compare it on the same outcome distribution.
analytical job: Test edge-to-edge descending stripes, center-out alternating stripes, and sight-scaled sinusoidal passes; measure 100-trial time distributions and interval overlap.
output: Systematic routes dominate random baselines; center-out spiral stripes give the lowest one-plane ideal-model times.
handoff: Discovery uncertainty tests whether the ideal-model winner remains preferable when passes can miss debris.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The same containment field and route family, now with separate radar and operator failure probabilities.
rhetorical job: Increase realism without losing comparability by changing the observation model and explicitly showing its effect on the next action.

analytical job: Set detection from radar and operator terms; update searched/unsearched containment after nondetection; choose posterior maxima for each pass; cap at 24 hours; compare 500 adaptive and fixed-route trials.
output: Bayesian search has a higher conditional mean but finds 95 percent by 24 hours versus 80 percent for fixed spiral stripes, with equal medians.
handoff: Stability scenarios alter target detectability and search resources before aggregate results choose a recommendation.
section_progressions.positive_pattern: Use the source-anchored input -> rhetorical job -> analytical job -> output -> handoff contract; warnings remain a last pass.

moves: input: The Bayesian winner, the ideal spiral/stripe geometry, Boeing target properties, and one P-8 search plane.
rhetorical job: Test flexibility by changing recognizable scenario dimensions instead of repeating the baseline with cosmetic inputs.
analytical job: Shrink the area and detection rate for a Cessna; then add a second plane with opposite, nonoverlapping striped motion; compare distributions and intervals.
output: Target size materially changes Bayesian search time, while a second idealized plane lowers stripe-search mean to about 2.4 hours.
handoff: Results synthesize all route and stability evidence by model regime.

moves: input: Seven ideal-route trials, three uncertain-discovery trials, confidence intervals, skew diagnostics, medians, and 24-hour failure counts.
rhetorical job: Prevent a single fast conditional mean from dominating by separating regimes and matching statistics to skew/censoring.
analytical job: Establish systematic-versus-random differences; identify two-plane and one-plane ideal winners; compare uncertain routes by median and completion proportion; compare target sizes.
output: Spiral stripes win the one-plane ideal model, but the Bayesian route wins the realistic decision because its equal median accompanies much higher completion.
handoff: Recommendation ties that statistical tradeoff back to the rescue-time criterion.

moves: input: Rescue-before-hypothermia criterion, ideal-route times, uncertain-route medians, and 24-hour completion proportions.
rhetorical job: Choose the most defensible route by the ranked objective rather than merely the smallest reported mean.
analytical job: Reject idealized solutions despite sub-eight-hour means; compare equal 4.05-hour medians; prefer 95-percent Bayesian completion over 80-percent spiral completion.
output: Recommend the normal distribution with discovery uncertainty paired with a Bayesian-adjusted flight path.
handoff: Strengths and weaknesses delimit what that recommendation actually supports.

moves: input: The chosen Bayesian mechanism, Boeing/Cessna completion evidence, confidence interval, and all earlier idealizations.
rhetorical job: Preserve the recommendation's adaptive value while preventing its modeled rescue performance from being mistaken for field validation.

analytical job: Attribute flexibility to adjustable detection/area/sight inputs; report completion and rescue-window evidence; identify exponential computation, overlap, distribution uncertainty, omitted drift/weather/debris stages, mobilization, fuel, and cost.
output: A bounded recommendation with explicit computational, geometric, physical, temporal, and resource failure modes.
handoff: The press document translates the intended procedure for a public audience while some technical caveats become less explicit.

moves: input: Public concern after MH370 and the paper's posterior-guided search loop.
rhetorical job: Translate technical work into accountable immediate actions without introducing a new mathematical claim.
analytical job: Predict from last signal/path; bound and deploy; fly parallel paths; update location from search data; adjust for equipment imperfections; continue and refine.
output: A stakeholder-facing commitment to rapid, thorough, adaptive searching.
handoff: References document the external evidence and software behind the technical paper.

moves: input: Historical cases, aircraft specifications, communication rules, search theory, radar tests, Bayesian formulas, visual-search evidence, survival data, images, and software.
rhetorical job: Expose the external basis of major choices while revealing what cannot be reconstructed from the paper alone.

main_argument_chains.claim: Aircraft state, failure-time uncertainty, glide geometry, and a nonuniform prior turn the open ocean into a bounded probability field.
support_steps: uniform x and normal y containment
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: candidate routes are compared on a bounded probability field rather than an unweighted ocean

main_argument_chains.claim: Successive baselines expose boundary and probability-order failures, leading to center-first systematic coverage under ideal detection.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: systematic center-first geometry is the best one-plane route under ideal detection

main_argument_chains.claim: Missed-detection Bayesian updates trade a higher success-conditional mean for materially greater 24-hour completion than a fixed spiral route.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Bayesian adaptive search is preferred despite a higher conditional mean

main_argument_chains.claim: Target/resource checks and the survival benchmark bound the recommendation as an adaptable modeled procedure rather than a field guarantee.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: the route is an adaptable modeled procedure, not a field guarantee

warnings.warning: Equation 2 multiplies a dimensionless glide ratio by altitude in feet but reports r in miles without an explicit feet-to-miles conversion. Preserve the source expression and require a typed conversion before numeric reuse.

Equation 4 visibly compares the vector difference S_i-(x_crash,y_crash) with scalar d without a norm, and the crash-coordinate notation conflicts with the earlier (x_c,y_c) table. A runnable detector needs a scalar distance and one coordinate contract.

Equations 6, 11, 13, and 16 advance the search plane with v even though v was defined for the lost aircraft and v_s for the search plane. The implementation must resolve the symbol rather than silently assuming 400 mph.

Equations 7, 8, and 12 use the set-union symbol between Boolean boundary conditions. Corner precedence, simultaneous x/y violations, and equality behavior are also omitted, so the printed rule is not an executable boundary contract.

The weighted random path fixes a factor of 15 without calibration or sensitivity analysis. Its confidence-interval overlap with bounded random is treated as no significant difference, although interval overlap is not the reported hypothesis test.

Equations 14 and 17 define C(u) as a dimensionless alternating integer while the route uses it as a physical stripe displacement. The visually printed formulas appear to omit a sight-range scale such as d.

Equation 15 does not make clear whether C(j) is an absolute vertical coordinate or an incremental displacement, nor whether j and epsilon update before or after the move. Preserve this ambiguity in any transcription.

Equation 18 adds scalar C(j)r to vector S_i, reuses r from lost-aircraft glide range, and flips epsilon although its downstream role is unclear. The printed transition is dimensionally and algorithmically incomplete.

The source rounds a cited 97-percent operator recognition probability to one, raising P(D_u) from about 0.776 to 0.8. Its minimum-90-second view claim assumes a full 20-mile diameter crossing and does not cover a marginal target encounter.

The Bayesian B777 interval is arithmetically inconsistent: 6.21463 plus or minus 2(0.246568) gives a lower bound about 5.72149, not 5.57215. The page also describes samples of size 100 although this run used 500 trials and 475 successes.

Uncertain-model means and intervals omit trials not found by 24 hours. Comparing Bayesian 95-percent completion with spiral 80-percent completion through success-conditional intervals does not compare overall time-to-discovery distributions; censoring or restricted-time analysis is required.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Ground the candidate-region discussion in the published MH370 search geometry and final satellite arc.

Define lost-aircraft timing, glide, path, and search-domain symbols before equations are introduced.
Define search-plane, sensor, crash-point, path-state, direction, endpoint-distance, and iteration notation.
Construct the rectangular search domain from the uncertain flight segment and two glide-radius endpoint circles.
Compare Boeing 777, Gulfstream G450, and Cessna 172 inputs and select the B777 baseline.
Show a richer path-and-endpoint containment pattern before replacing it with a tractable distribution.
Visualize the simplified prior that is uniform along the flight direction and Gaussian across it.
Provide sensor context beside the P-8/P-3 radar discussion.
Compare P-3 and P-8 search resources and fix the P-8 simulation baseline.
Check that the crash sampler follows the selected center-weighted containment field.
Explain how a random vector is normalized to generate one route increment.
Show why an unconstrained random walk can leave the probability field and fail to finish.
Explain the horizontal and vertical center-return vectors used after a boundary crossing.
Show the boundary-corrected random route remaining inside the candidate domain.
Expose the highly right-skewed distribution of bounded-random completion times.
Show how a random direction and a farther-endpoint direction are combined.
Show a stochastic route biased toward the path endpoints and central probability band.
Compare weighted-random time shape with the prior random baselines.
Explain center-start horizontal stripes that descend by one radar diameter at each turn.
Show a simulated discovery along the deterministic descending-stripe route.
Summarize systematic-stripe discovery times under ideal detection.
Explain how alternating center-out stripe order targets the highest Gaussian mass first.
Show a simulated discovery along the center-out alternating route.
Summarize the paper's strongest ideal one-plane route.
Explain the tangent-stepped sine route and alternating vertical transitions.
Show one simulated discovery on the sinusoidal center-out route.
Summarize ideal-detection performance of the sinusoidal alternative.
Define radar, operator, total discovery, searched-cell, and alternative-cell probabilities before Bayesian updating.
Show the initial Gaussian cross-track and uniform along-track grid before any search pass.
Provide a plan-view counterpart to the three-dimensional prior.
Show how a missed central search depresses visited probability and shifts the next priorities to y=+/-20 miles.
Continue the adaptive update and identify the next most probable stripe.
Summarize adaptive-search times among successful trials and report the 24-hour completion proportion.
Compare the fixed spiral path under the same imperfect-discovery setting.
Check limited target-size and search-area transfer for the Bayesian route.
Show how two aircraft divide systematic stripe coverage.
Summarize the resource extension from one to two search aircraft.
Compare the bounded and weighted random-route mean intervals.
Place systematic ideal-route intervals on a common visual scale.
Compare conditional successful-trial times for Bayesian and fixed spiral routes under imperfect discovery.
Relate modeled discovery times to the recommendation's 18-hour rescue benchmark.
